api.error.requestFailed: Error shown when the server rejected a request without its own message. {status} is the HTTP status code, e.g. 500.
appearance.languageLabel: Label of the language menu. The menu lists every language in its own name and is never translated.
appearance.mode.dark.label: Mode segment. Very short.
appearance.mode.light.label: One segment of a four-way switch (Light / Medium / Dark / System) in a narrow popover. Very short.
appearance.mode.medium.label: Mode segment: soft dark. Very short.
appearance.mode.system.label: Mode segment: follow the operating system. Very short.
appearance.modeLegend: Heading above the Light / Medium / Dark / System switch.
appearance.scheme.observatory.label: Name of a colour scheme. These five are product names for palettes: translate them only if your market would; otherwise keep the English word.
appearance.scheme.void.description: 'Vercel-like' compares it to Vercel's website. Keep 'Vercel'.
appearance.scheme.warm.description: 'the Claude palette' names Claude, the AI assistant's colours. Keep 'Claude'.
appearance.schemeLegend: Heading above the colour-scheme cards. 'Scheme' means a colour palette.
appearance.summary: Small line under the popover's title: the current colour scheme and mode, both already translated.
appearance.trigger.srLabel: Screen-reader name of the same button. {scheme} is a colour-scheme name (Observatory, Dim…) and {mode} a mode name (Light, Dark, System), both already translated.
appearance.trigger.title: Tooltip on the header button (a palette icon) that opens the Appearance popover.
atlas.canvasLabel: Screen-reader label of the atlas canvas. {count} is the number of cards, each drawn as a building in a city.
atlas.control.export: Screen-reader label of an icon button (⤓) that saves the map as an image.
atlas.control.fit: Screen-reader label of an icon button (⤢) that zooms out so the whole city fits.
atlas.engine.flat.label: Small segmented button, top-right: draw the city with flat 2D shading. One short word.
atlas.engine.flat.title: Tooltip of the Flat button.
atlas.engine.group: Screen-reader label of the two-button switch for how the city is drawn (flat 2D shading vs 3D).
atlas.engine.lit.label: Small segmented button, top-right: draw the city in lit 3D. Keep it as short as '3D'.
atlas.engine.lit.title: Tooltip of the 3D button.
atlas.inside.back: Button in a small chip, shown after clicking into a building; returns to the whole city. Keep the arrow.
atlas.legend: One-line keyboard and mouse hint along the bottom edge of the map, shown in uppercase. → and ← are the arrow keys. Keep it short; it truncates.
atlas.lens.degree.hint: Hubs = cards with many connections; towers = tall buildings.
atlas.lens.degree.label: Lens option: building height by number of connections. Dropdown about 10rem wide.
atlas.lens.drift.hint: 'Bound code' = source files linked to the card. 'Scaffolded' = drawn with a scaffolding cage, meaning drifted.
atlas.lens.drift.label: Lens option: show cards whose code changed since the card was last verified ('drift'). Dropdown about 10rem wide.
atlas.lens.label: Small uppercase label before the lens dropdown. A lens is the question the map answers (height and colour of buildings).
atlas.lens.recency.label: Lens option: building height by how recently the card was edited. Dropdown about 10rem wide.
atlas.lens.size.hint: FILE is a card type name; keep it as is.
atlas.lens.size.label: Lens option: building height by lines of code. Dropdown about 10rem wide.
atlas.lens.status.hint: Explanation shown next to the dropdown when this lens is picked. The colon followed by a dash is intentional in English; a legend sits there.
atlas.lens.status.label: Lens option in a dropdown about 10rem wide: colour buildings by card status.
atlas.readout.drifted: Hover readout for a building whose linked code changed since the card was verified.
atlas.readout.driftedWithParts: Same as atlas.readout.drifted, followed by {parts} = the text of atlas.readout.parts.
atlas.readout.parts: Hover readout for a building. {count} is how many parts (files, functions or sections) it has; {names} is a list of the first few part names (plan data).
atlas.readout.partsMore: Same as atlas.readout.parts, but the card has more than three parts and only three are named, so the list ends with an ellipsis.
atlas.trace.at: Shown at the right of the trace controls: the building (card) the current step happens at. {handle} is a card id like API-TICKETS, drawn as a chip.
atlas.trace.close: Screen-reader label of the ✕ button that closes the flow-trace panel.
atlas.trace.pause: Same button while playing; stops auto-advance. Keep short.
atlas.trace.play: Button that auto-advances through the flow's steps. Small button; keep short.
atlas.trace.region: Screen-reader label of the panel that walks through a FLOW card step by step on the map.
atlas.trace.step: Step counter, e.g. '3/7'. {step} is the current step number, {total} the number of steps.
board.column.building.empty: Italic hint in the empty Building column ('in flight' = currently being worked on).
board.column.building.title: Kanban column heading for cards whose status is 'building' (work in progress). Keep short.
board.column.built.empty: Italic hint in the empty Built column.
board.column.built.title: Kanban column heading for cards whose status is 'built' (done, not yet verified). Keep short.
board.column.emptyFallback: Italic hint in an empty Kanban column that declares no hint of its own.
board.column.planned.empty: Italic hint in the empty Planned column.
board.column.planned.title: Kanban column heading for cards whose status is 'planned'. Column is 18rem wide, next to a count badge — keep short. Capitalised heading form of status.planned.
board.column.verified.empty: Italic hint in the empty Verified column.
board.column.verified.title: Kanban column heading for cards whose status is 'verified' (built and checked). Keep short.
board.dialog.close: Accessible name of the ✕ button and the backdrop that close the card preview dialog.
board.dialog.connectionCount: Footer of the preview dialog, small monospace text. {count} is the number of cards connected to this one.
board.dialog.connections: Small uppercase heading above the list of connected cards in the preview dialog.
board.dialog.noBody: Italic placeholder in the card preview when the card has no markdown body.
board.dialog.notFound: Shown in the preview dialog when the URL names a card that does not exist. {handle} is a card identifier such as API-TICKETS.
board.dialog.openCard: Footer link from the preview dialog to the card's full page. The arrow is decorative.
board.empty.description: Empty-state body below board.empty.title. FEATURE is a card type prefix — keep it. {path} is a file path pattern (feature/FEATURE-*.md).
board.empty.title: Heading of the empty state when the plan has no FEATURE cards. FEATURE is a card type prefix — keep it as written.
board.kanban.defaultLabel: Fallback accessible name of a Kanban board region when the caller gives none. Not shown on screen.
board.label: Accessible name (aria-label) of the Kanban board region holding every FEATURE card. Not shown on screen.
board.overflow: Link at the foot of the Verified column, which shows at most 20 cards. {count} is how many more verified cards are hidden; the link opens the full list.
board.tasks.blurb.board: One-line description under the Tasks heading on the board tab. FEATURE is a card type prefix — keep it. {field} is the frontmatter key 'status:' and stays as written.
board.tasks.blurb.list: One-line description under the Tasks heading on the list tab. 'Release provenance' = which release shipped each feature. FEATURE is a card type prefix — keep it.
board.tasks.tab.board: Tab label: the Kanban board view. Tabs are narrow — one short word.
board.tasks.tab.list: Tab label: the list view. Tabs are narrow — one short word.
board.tasks.title: Page heading of the Tasks area (the board and list views of FEATURE cards).
card.connections.add: Small dashed ghost button that adds a connection to another card. The leading + means "add". Monospace.
card.connections.addPlaceholder: Placeholder of the input where the user types another card's handle (an uppercase identifier like API-TICKETS). Monospace; uppercase reads as a code token.
card.connections.removeLabel: Screen-reader label for the × button. {handle} is the connected card's identifier.
card.connections.removeTitle: Tooltip on the small × that removes one connection chip.
card.connections.unknownTarget: Error toast. {handle} is a card identifier (e.g. API-TICKETS) the user typed that does not exist.
card.create.description: Help line under the dialog title. A handle is the card's identifier (e.g. API-TICKETS); the type prefix is the part before the first dash.
card.create.errorInvalid: Inline form error. Handles may only contain A–Z, 0–9 and dashes — keep those characters literally.
card.create.handleLabel: Form label. "Handle" is Constellation's term for a card's unique identifier (e.g. API-TICKETS).
card.create.handlePlaceholder: Example handle suffix typed after a fixed prefix like "API-". Must stay uppercase A–Z/0–9/dashes; you may keep it as-is.
card.create.nameLabel: Form label for the card's optional human-readable display name.
card.create.namePlaceholder: Placeholder of the display-name input: a short description of the card.
card.create.optional: Faint tag after the Name label meaning the field may be left empty.
card.create.preview: Live preview line under the form. {handle} (shown bold) is the handle that will be created, e.g. API-NEW-TICKET.
card.create.title: Dialog title. {type} is the card type as an in-sentence noun ("feature", "API endpoint", "database table").
card.create.titleNoType: Dialog title when the type is unknown.
card.delete.confirm: Destructive confirm button in the delete dialog.
card.delete.doneDangling.multiple: Toast after deleting {handle}. {handles} is a comma-separated list of two or more cards whose connections now point at nothing.
card.delete.doneDangling.single: Toast after deleting {handle}. {handles} is the ONE card whose connection now points at nothing (conjugate for a singular subject).
card.delete.referenced.multiple: Delete dialog text. {handle} is the card; {handles} is a comma-separated list of two or more cards connected to it.
card.delete.referenced.single: Delete dialog text. {handle} is the card; {handles} is the ONE card connected to it.
card.delete.referencedAt.multiple: As card.delete.referenced.multiple, plus {path}: the card's file path (e.g. api/API-TICKETS.md).
card.delete.referencedAt.single: As card.delete.referenced.single, plus {path}: the card's file path (e.g. api/API-TICKETS.md).
card.delete.title: Confirmation dialog title. {handle} is the card identifier.
card.delete.unreferencedAt: {path} is the card's file path (e.g. api/API-TICKETS.md).
card.fields.add: Small dashed ghost button that adds a frontmatter field. The leading + means "add". Monospace.
card.fields.addPlaceholder: Placeholder of a one-line input where the user types a new field as YAML `key: value`. Keep the colon syntax; translate only the words key/value if your language would.
card.fields.invalidYaml: Error toast: the typed field value is not valid YAML, so nothing was saved. YAML is a format name — do not translate.
card.list.empty: Shown in a card list that has no cards of this type yet.
card.list.filterPlaceholder: Placeholder of the search box that filters the card list. Narrow column (~16rem).
card.list.new: Button at the bottom of a card list that creates a card. {type} is the type as an in-sentence lowercase-ish noun ("feature", "API endpoint"). The leading + means "add".
card.notFound.description: {handle} is a card identifier from the URL, e.g. API-TICKETS.
card.page.bodyPlaceholder: Placeholder shown where an empty card's markdown body would be; click to start writing. The leading + means "add".
card.page.delete: Small lowercase text button in a card page's header, shown on hover; opens the delete confirmation. Verb. Keep short.
card.page.kindPlaceholder: Placeholder of the inline editor for a card's `kind` (a free-form subtype like "endpoint"). The leading + means "add". Monospace, small.
card.section.connections: Small uppercase section heading above the chips linking this card to other cards.
card.section.fields: Small uppercase section heading above a card's frontmatter fields (key/value pairs).
card.typeIntro.count: Small monospace count under a card type's name, e.g. "3 cards".
card.unknownType: Shown when the URL names a card folder that does not exist. {folder} is the raw folder name from the URL (e.g. "apis").
docs.card.openSource: Tooltip on a card's handle link inside the document. {handle} is the card identifier, e.g. DOC-FILE-FORMAT.
docs.defaultTitle: Title of the compiled document when the plan does not set one.
docs.empty.description: Body of that empty state. {field} is the frontmatter key 'section:', {listField} the key 'doc_sections:', {handle} the card identifier PLAN-PROJECT — all stay as written. A 'slug' is a short identifier.
docs.empty.title: Heading of the empty state when the plan has no documentation sections.
docs.empty.unknownSection: Body when the URL names a section no card declares. {field} is the frontmatter key 'section:' (stays as written); {section} is the section id from the URL.
docs.empty.unknownTitle: Heading when the URL names a documentation section that does not exist.
docs.export.blockedMessage: Toast body under docs.export.blockedTitle. {shortcut} is the keyboard shortcut ⌘P. “Save as PDF” is the browser's own print-dialog option — use the wording browsers show in your language.
docs.export.blockedTitle: Toast title when the browser blocked the print window from opening.
docs.export.button: Small button on the document cover that opens a print window for saving as PDF.
docs.eyebrow: Small label above the compiled document's title, on its cover.
docs.imprint: Cover line under the document title. {version} is the package version number (the 'v' prefix stands for 'version'); {date} is today's date, already formatted.
docs.print.action: Large button in the print window that opens the browser's print dialog (verb).
docs.print.empty: Shown in the print window when there is nothing to print. {field} is the frontmatter key 'section:' and stays as written.
docs.print.hint.partial: Hint beside the Print button when some diagrams failed to render before the time limit.
docs.print.hint.ready: Hint beside the Print button once ready. “Save as PDF” is the browser's own print-dialog option — use the wording browsers show in your language.
docs.print.hint.waiting: Hint beside the Print button while the diagrams render.
docs.print.preparing: Same button while diagrams are still rendering; it is disabled.
docs.print.windowTitle: Second part of the print window's tab title, after the document title ('My project · Print'). It also becomes the default PDF file name.
docs.toc.empty: Shown in the contents rail when no card belongs to a section. {field} is the frontmatter key 'section:' and stays as written.
docs.toc.heading: Heading of the table of contents (in the side rail and on the printed contents page); also its accessible name on the printed page.
docs.toc.jumpLabel: Accessible label of the drop-down that jumps to a section on narrow screens.
docs.toc.jumpPlaceholder: Placeholder of that drop-down before a section is picked.
docs.toc.navLabel: Accessible name of the table-of-contents navigation in the side rail.
docs.toc.wholeDocument: Link in the contents rail back from one section to the whole document. Rail is 13rem wide.
edit.emptyPlaceholder: Faint italic placeholder for an empty editable value.
edit.hint: Tiny monospace hint under a multi-line inline editor. Keep the key glyphs ⌘↩ and esc; translate only "save" and "cancel". Keep it short — one line.
edit.toast.readonly: Error toast: the viewer server runs in read-only mode.
edit.toast.saveFailed: Fallback error toast when the server gave no message.
edit.toast.stale: Error toast: the card file was changed by something else since it was loaded, so the save was refused and the page reloaded.
edit.toast.syncPoint: Success toast. {sha} is a short git commit id (8 hex characters).
features.empty: Empty state of the feature list. FEATURE is a card type prefix — keep it. {path} is a file path pattern shown as code.
features.pr.link: Compact chip linking to a pull request on GitHub. 'PR' = pull request; ↗ marks an external link. Keep as short as possible.
features.pr.number: Compact chip naming a pull request. {pr} is the PR number or id from the card. Keep short.
features.section.shipped: Small uppercase section heading: features that are built or verified. A count follows it.
features.section.upNext: Small uppercase section heading: features not yet built (planned, building, or no status). A count follows it.
features.sectionEmpty: Italic hint under a feature-list section heading that has no cards.
graph.canvasLabel: Screen-reader label of the graph canvas. {count} is the number of cards drawn. Escape is the keyboard key; keep the key name as is.
graph.control.fit: Tooltip and screen-reader label of an icon button (⤢) that zooms so the whole graph fits the screen.
graph.control.reset: Tooltip of an icon button (⟲) that resets the camera. One short word.
graph.control.resetLabel: Screen-reader label of the same reset button (⟲): resets the camera position and zoom.
graph.panel.open: Link in the small pill shown under a selected card; opens the card's page. Keep the arrow. Short — the pill is one line.
graph.search.placeholder: Placeholder of the search box floating over the graph. 'Nodes' are the cards drawn as boxes.
graph.tabs.atlas.hint: Tooltip of the Atlas button. 'Isometric' is the 3D drawing style.
graph.tabs.atlas.label: Segmented button, top-left over the canvas: the plan drawn as an isometric city (atlas = a book of maps). One short word.
graph.tabs.graph.label: Segmented button, top-left over the canvas: the force-directed node graph. One short word.
graph.tabs.group: Screen-reader label of the two-button switch between the Graph and Atlas readings of the plan.
home.activity.kind.code: Tiny uppercase tag on a commit row (fixed width, about 5 characters): the commit changed source code.
home.activity.kind.plan: Tiny uppercase tag on a commit row (fixed width, about 5 characters): the commit changed plan cards.
home.activity.moreCards: After two card IDs on a commit row: how many more cards the commit touched ('+3').
home.activity.syncTag: Tiny uppercase pill on the commit that is the plan's sync point.
home.activity.title: Panel heading on the overview, small uppercase: recent git commits.
home.countValue: Just the number; the code uses it to find the count inside counted text. Copy exactly as is: {count}
home.drift.baseline.argument: On a drifted card's row: changed since an explicitly given base commit.
home.drift.baseline.cardCommit: On a drifted card's row: changed since the card file's last git commit.
home.drift.baseline.fallback: On a drifted card's row: changed since its (unspecified) baseline.
home.drift.baseline.syncMarker: On a drifted card's row: changed since the plan's sync point.
home.drift.baseline.verified: On a drifted card's row: changed since the card was last verified against the code.
home.drift.claimsDrifted: Drift panel verdict (amber). {drifted} cards out of {count} tracked cards have code that changed.
home.drift.claimsHold: Drift panel verdict (green): every tracked card still matches its code. A 'claim' is a card describing code.
home.drift.filesChanged: On a drifted card's row: how many bound files changed. Followed by ' · ' and one of home.drift.baseline.*.
home.drift.nothingTracked: Drift panel verdict when no card has a baseline to compare against yet.
home.drift.overflow: Below the capped list of drifted cards: how many more are not listed.
home.drift.title: Panel heading on the overview, small uppercase: cards whose bound code changed.
home.drift.untracked: Footnote in the drift panel. {count} is shown bold; {hint} is home.drift.untrackedHint.
home.drift.untrackedHint: Inserted at the end of home.drift.untracked. 'them' = the cards with no baseline. {tool} is the tool name 'set_verified' — keep as is.
home.health.chip.cards: Tiny uppercase label next to a number in the health strip ('42 CARDS'). Shown for any count; use a plural/collective form. Keep very short.
home.health.chip.clean: Shown in the number slot (bold) when there are no lint errors, above/next to the label 'integrity'. One short word.
home.health.chip.code: Tiny uppercase label after 'no drift' — reads 'no drift · code'. The source code, not a code number.
home.health.chip.connections: Tiny uppercase label next to the number of links between cards ('97 CONNECTIONS'). Shown for any count. Keep very short.
home.health.chip.drifted: Tiny uppercase label next to the number of cards whose code changed since they were verified.
home.health.chip.errors: Health strip chip: a lint error count ('2 ERRORS'). The number is shown big and bold before the remaining words, which become a tiny uppercase label — keep them short.
home.health.chip.integrity: Tiny uppercase label under 'clean': the plan's structural integrity (no broken links). One short word.
home.health.chip.noDrift: Shown in the number slot (bold) when no card's code has drifted, next to the label 'code'. Very short.
home.health.chip.untracked: Tiny uppercase label next to the number of cards with no drift baseline yet.
home.health.chip.warnings: Health strip chip: a lint warning count. The number is shown big and bold before the remaining words, which become a tiny uppercase label.
home.health.codeCommits: Count of git commits that changed code since the sync point. Inserted into home.health.sinceMarker.
home.health.lastSynced: Small grey status line in the overview's health strip. {when} is a relative time already in your language ('4m ago', 'just now'). Lowercase sentence fragment; parts are joined with ' · '.
home.health.noSyncPoint: Health strip status line when the plan was never stamped with a sync point (a git commit marking 'the plan was true here'). Lowercase fragment.
home.health.planChanges: Count of plan (card) changes since the sync point. Inserted into home.health.sinceMarker.
home.health.planDirty: Health strip fragment: the plan folder has edits not yet committed to git.
home.health.setSyncPoint: Small button in the health strip: record the current git commit as the plan's sync point (first time).
home.health.sinceMarker: Health strip, after 'last synced …'. {commits} is home.health.codeCommits and {changes} is home.health.planChanges, both already counted ('3 code commits'). 'since' = since the sync point.
home.health.updateSyncPoint: Small button in the health strip: move the existing sync point to the current git commit.
home.noPlan: Overview page, shown when the plan has no root file. {file} is the file name 'plan.md' and {command} is the CLI command 'constellation init' — both stay as they are. Keep the backticks around {command}.
home.notes.empty: Empty state of the Notes panel. {tool} is the tool name 'append_note', shown as code — keep as is.
home.notes.kind.decision: Kind of a note on a card, shown in a narrow column (about 8 characters, truncates). A decision that was made.
home.notes.kind.deviation: Kind of a note on a card, shown in a narrow column. Where the code departs from the plan.
home.notes.kind.gotcha: Kind of a note on a card, shown in a narrow column. A pitfall / trap to watch out for.
home.notes.kind.state: Kind of a note on a card, shown in a narrow column. The current state of the work.
home.notes.kind.verified: Kind of a note on a card, shown in a narrow column. A record that the card was checked against the code.
home.notes.title: Panel heading on the overview, small uppercase: recent notes left on cards.
home.releases.breakingCount: Tiny uppercase pill / summary piece: number of breaking changes in a release ('2 breaking'). Adjective used as a noun; keep short.
home.releases.empty: Empty state of the Releases panel. RELEASE and FEATURE are card type names — keep them in capitals. {releaseField} and {changeField} are the field names 'release:' and 'change:', shown as code.
home.releases.group.breaking: Small uppercase group heading in a release: breaking changes.
home.releases.group.chore: Small uppercase group heading in a release: maintenance/housekeeping work.
home.releases.group.feature: Small uppercase group heading in a release: new features.
home.releases.group.fix: Small uppercase group heading in a release: bug fixes.
home.releases.latestTag: {tag} is the newest git tag, e.g. 'v1.2.0'. Means: this version has been tagged in git.
home.releases.noFeatures: Expanded release with no FEATURE cards pointing at it. FEATURE is a card type name — keep in capitals.
home.releases.noTags: Releases panel: the repo has no git tags and no package version.
home.releases.open: Link at the bottom of an expanded release. {handle} is a card ID like RELEASE-V1-2-0. Keep the arrow.
home.releases.packageVersion: {version} is the version string from {file} (always 'package.json', keep as is).
home.releases.summary.features: Right-aligned grey summary on a shipped release: how many features it contained.
home.releases.summary.noFeatures: Right-aligned grey summary on a release row that has no features yet.
home.releases.summary.progress: Right-aligned grey summary on a release in progress. {shipped} is how many are done, {count} the total.
home.releases.summary.shipped: Right-aligned grey summary on a release row with no features, when the release has shipped.
home.releases.tagged: Tiny uppercase pill on a release row: this version has a matching git tag.
home.releases.title: Panel heading on the overview, small uppercase.
home.repos.cardCount: Right side of a connected-repo row: how many cards that repo's plan has.
home.repos.current: Right side of a connected-repo row: this row is the workspace you are viewing now.
home.repos.hint: Small grey footnote under the connected repos list. 'switcher' = the workspace menu at the top of the sidebar.
home.repos.notServed: Right side of a connected-repo row: this viewer cannot open that repo's plan.
home.repos.title: Section heading on the overview, small uppercase: other repositories linked to this plan.
nav.constellation: Sidebar row and page title for the graph/atlas page. 'Constellation' is also the product name; keep it unless a common translation of the word reads better as a page name. Narrow sidebar row.
nav.docs: Sidebar row and page title: the compiled documentation of the project. Narrow sidebar row.
nav.drawer.close: Accessible name of the X button that closes the phone navigation sheet.
nav.drawer.title: Hidden heading (screen readers only) of the slide-out navigation sheet on phones.
nav.overview: Sidebar row and page title: the project's dashboard page. The sidebar row is narrow (about 20 characters before it truncates).
nav.planLabel: Accessible name (screen readers only) of the left navigation rail and the phone drawer's list.
nav.styleGuide: Sidebar row, page title and command-palette entry: the page that shows the project's design tokens. Narrow sidebar row.
nav.tasks: Sidebar row and page title: the board/list of features in flight. Narrow sidebar row.
palette.empty: Shown in the command palette when nothing matches what was typed.
palette.group.goTo: Group heading in the command palette above the app's pages (navigation targets).
palette.group.scheme: Group heading in the command palette above the colour schemes. Same meaning as the Appearance popover's 'Scheme' legend. Also used as a search word for those rows.
palette.hint.active: Small right-aligned hint on the colour scheme currently in use. Short.
palette.keyword.page: Not shown: a search word that matches every page entry in the command palette. One lowercase word for 'page'.
palette.label: Accessible name of the ⌘K command palette dialog.
palette.page.atlas: Command palette entry: the Constellation page drawn as a city map (the 'atlas').
palette.page.graph: Command palette entry: the Constellation page drawn as a node graph. Should match nav.constellation.
palette.page.tasksBoard: Command palette entry: the Tasks page in its board (kanban) view. 'Tasks' should match nav.tasks.
palette.page.tasksList: Command palette entry: the Tasks page in its list view.
palette.placeholder: Placeholder of the command palette's search input. Cards are the plan's documents; pages are the app's pages.
shell.header.openNav: Accessible name of the hamburger button that opens the navigation sheet on phones.
shell.header.openRepo: Accessible name of the GitHub icon link in the header. GitHub is a brand name.
shell.header.searchLabel: Accessible name of the header's search button, which opens the command palette.
shell.header.searchPlaceholder: Placeholder-like text inside the header search button (truncates; about 25 characters fit).
status.building: A card's status: work in progress. Short, one word.
status.built: A card's status: implemented. Short, one word.
status.none: Option in the status menu that clears a card's status.
status.planned: A card's status. Shown in a small pill that is often uppercased by CSS; keep it one short word, lowercase where the language allows.
status.verified: A card's status: implemented and checked against the code. Short, one word.
style.fontStyles: Small heading above a list mapping font token names to CSS font stacks.
style.guide.emptyDescription: Empty-state help. style/ is a folder name and "tokens"/"category" are field names — keep them as-is.
style.guide.emptyTitle: Empty-state title. STYLE is a card type prefix — keep it as-is.
style.specimen.characters: Tiny label above a row of punctuation/symbol characters in a font specimen.
style.specimen.lowercase: Tiny label above a row of a–z sample letters in a font specimen.
style.specimen.numbers: Tiny label above the digits 0–9 in a font specimen.
style.specimen.uppercase: Tiny label above a row of A–Z sample letters in a font specimen.
style.typeScale.sample: Sample sentence rendered at each size of a type scale. Use your language's pangram or any natural sentence of similar length.
sync.badge.cardsAhead: Muted text inside the 'Drifted' badge: how many plan cards changed since the last sync. {count} is the number. Short.
sync.badge.commitsBehind: Muted text inside the 'Drifted' badge: how many code commits landed since the plan was last synced. {count} is the number. Short; may be joined to the next item with ' · '.
sync.badge.markerUnreachable: Muted text inside the 'Drifted' badge: the git commit the plan was last synced at can no longer be found. Lowercase, short.
sync.badge.title: Tooltip on the freshness badge in the header. Clicking the badge opens the Overview dashboard.
sync.state.dirty: Freshness verdict: the plan folder has edits not yet committed to git. Short.
sync.state.drifted: Freshness verdict: code changed since the plan was last synced to it. Short.
sync.state.inSync: The plan's freshness verdict: the plan cards were reviewed against the latest code. Shown in a small badge in the header and on the dashboard. Short.
sync.state.neverSynced: Freshness verdict: nobody has ever marked the plan as synced to the code. Short.
time.justNow: Relative time for something that happened under a minute ago, in the same lowercase style as '5m ago' (which the browser formats).
types.agent.name: Sidebar section holding rules written for AI coding agents.
types.db.name: Sidebar section holding database table cards. 'single' is one table.
types.diagram.name: Sidebar section holding architecture diagram cards. 'single' is one diagram card.
types.external.name: Sidebar section holding cards for third-party services the project calls.
types.file.name: Sidebar section holding cards that each describe one file in the code repository.
types.group.code: Small uppercase sidebar group heading: repo files and tests.
types.group.interface: Small uppercase sidebar group heading: pages, components, style.
types.group.system: Small uppercase sidebar group heading: the back-end types (API, DB, events, jobs…).
types.plan.name: Section name in the sidebar and the card-type label for the 'Plans' card type (the plan's root card).
types.plan.single: One card of this type as a noun used INSIDE a sentence ('+ new {type}', 'New {type} card'). Lowercase in English except acronyms. Every types.*.single key works the same way: use your language's normal noun form and capitalisation.
types.state.name: Sidebar section holding state-machine cards.
types.style.name: Sidebar section holding design-token cards (colours, type, spacing).
ui.alertDialog.confirm: Default confirm button of a confirmation dialog when the app gives no label. Short button.
ui.command.empty: Default text when a command palette search has no results.
ui.command.label: Default accessible name of a command palette dialog.
ui.command.placeholder: Default placeholder of a command palette's search input.
ui.search.clear: Accessible name of the X button that empties a search field.
ui.search.placeholder: Default placeholder of a search field.
ui.select.placeholder: Default text of a dropdown before anything is chosen.
ui.sidebar.collapse: Tooltip and accessible name of the rail's edge toggle when the rail is expanded.
ui.sidebar.defaultLabel: Default accessible name of a navigation rail when the app gives none. Rarely heard.
ui.sidebar.expand: Tooltip and accessible name of the rail's edge toggle when the rail is collapsed to icons.
ui.splitPanel.resize: Accessible name of the draggable divider between the card list and the card.
ui.toaster.label: Accessible name of the region where pop-up notifications appear.
workspace.fallbackName: Name shown at the top of the rail when the project has no name yet. Short (one word ideally).
workspace.group.connected: Small heading in the workspace switcher above plans from other repositories linked to this one.
workspace.group.self: Small heading in the workspace switcher above the plans in the current git repository.
workspace.listLabel: Accessible name of the workspace switcher's popup list. A workspace is one plan the viewer can open (this repo's or a connected repo's).
workspace.unavailable: Muted line under a connected repository the server could not open, when it gave no reason.
